e.l: Do I need a permit for the peak?
e.a: 🌋 Yes. The final stretch, from La Rambleta to the crater (trail PNT 10 Telesforo Bravo), can only be walked with a prior authorisation, and going up without one can end in a fine. The permit is valid only for that stretch, that day and that time slot, and none are issued between 22:00 and 6:00. Under the Cabildo’s resolution of 14 October 2026, trails PNT 07 (Montaña Blanca), PNT 09 (Pico Viejo), PNT 23 (Los Regatones Negros) and PNT 28 (Chafarí) also need booking in advance.

e.l: Where do I book the permit?
e.a: 📅 On Tenerife ON (tenerifeon.es), the Cabildo’s official platform. You have to register first, it is free. Slots open every Monday at 07:00 Canary time for the following 56 days, and only one booking per person every 15 days is allowed. They go fast: be there first thing on Monday.

k: do i pay for the permit
e.l: Is the permit free?
e.a: 💶 It depends on the trail and the time. Only PNT 10 (the summit one) and PNT 07 (Montaña Blanca) have a fee, and only from 9:00 to 17:00, the hours that match the cable car. On PNT 10, residents in Tenerife and children under 14 pay nothing and everyone else does, with one amount for residents elsewhere in the Canaries and another for all other visitors; on PNT 07 the amount also changes between weekdays and weekends or public holidays. Outside those hours, and on PNT 09, 23 and 28, there is no fee, but booking is still compulsory. Tenerife ON shows you the exact amount as you book, and you can ask for a refund if the trail is closed or the cable car is not running, or if you ask three or more days in advance.

k: does the cable car reach the peak
how high does the cable car go
e.l: Does the cable car reach the peak?
e.a: ❌ No, and this is the costliest misunderstanding on the Teide. The ticket leaves you at La Rambleta, around 3,555 m; to carry on to the crater you need the PNT 10 permit, booked separately and not included. They are two independent things: in fact your permit is valid for its slot even if the cable car is not running that day.

e.l: How does the cable car work?
e.a: 🚡 It climbs from around 2,356 m to La Rambleta, about 3,555 m, in some eight minutes. Worth buying ahead because it sells out, and it closes with no warning in strong wind or ice. Check the day’s status on volcanoteide.com before driving up: it saves you a wasted trip.

e.l: Can I walk up?
e.a: 🥾 Yes. You can reach La Rambleta on foot via Montaña Blanca (PNT 07), via Pico Viejo and Las Narices del Teide (PNT 09) or from Los Roques de García; the stratovolcano trails also require prior authorisation. And from there, the final stretch to the crater still needs the PNT 10 permit. Nothing is improvised here: it is all booked in advance.

e.l: How long and how hard?
e.a: ⏱️ The final stretch is barely 0.66 km, but it takes close to an hour: it starts around 3,542 m, ends at 3,714 m and has slopes of up to 60 %. Officially it is medium difficulty, although at that altitude your body delivers half of what it normally does. Not suitable if you have heart, breathing or mobility problems.

e.l: Is there a park entrance fee?
e.a: 🎟️ No. The park is open: you can drive the road, stop at the viewpoints and walk most trails without paying anything. What has to be booked are the stratovolcano trails: PNT 10, PNT 07, PNT 09, PNT 23 and PNT 28; of these, only PNT 10 and PNT 07 require payment, and only from 9:00 to 17:00. And note: Tenerife ON reminds visitors that smoking is banned in the National Park, vapes and e-cigarettes included.

e.l: What should I wear? Is it cold?
e.a: 🧥 It is far colder up there than on the coast, and the peak trail has mandatory kit: proper mountain footwear, long trousers (worn or in your pack) and a fleece or warm layer. Without it, the control staff will not let you up. Add a hat, sunglasses, sunscreen, water and something to eat.

e.l: Does altitude sickness hit?
e.a: 🫁 It can. At 3,700 m there is close to half the oxygen you get at sea level, and fatigue, headache and dizziness are normal, especially if you take the cable car and start walking right away. Go slowly, stop often, drink water and do not arrive on an empty stomach or hungover. If you really feel bad, go down.

e.l: Snow? Do roads close?
e.a: ❄️ It can snow in winter, and the Cabildo closes the park roads when there is ice: check road status before setting off. If there is snow or ice on the peak trail, the booking also demands crampons and an ice axe plus a declaration of high-mountain experience. Check the AEMET high-mountain forecast too, which is not the one for the village below.

e.l: Can I sleep in the refuge?
e.a: 🏔️ The Altavista refuge, at around 3,260 m, is the classic way to sleep up high and reach the summit early. Its opening times, prices and booking method change with the season, so check them on its website before building your plan around it. The other way to spend the night up there is to bivouac: above 2,500 m there are areas that must be booked in advance on Tenerife ON, such as the one on Guajara mountain. Other than that, camping and sleeping in a car or a motorhome are not allowed in the park.

e.l: Where do I see the stars?
e.a: ✨ Las Cañadas has one of the best skies in Europe. To watch the stars on your own you need no permit: park at a viewpoint in the park, wrap up properly and wait for the valley lights to fade; a telescope, only at the spots the park allows. Guided stargazing is booked separately, and the Teide Observatory is visited by day, with a guide and a prior booking: there are no night visits, and children under 8 are not admitted. In the app, the 🔭 at the top tells you what you can see each night, and «Where to go» has the places to watch from and the National Park rules for the night.

e.l: Can I go with kids?
e.a: 👨‍👩‍👧 To the park and the cable car, yes, allowing for the cold and the altitude. To the peak trail, not entirely: under-3s are not allowed, and under-16s must always be accompanied by an adult. For them the La Rambleta viewpoints and the Los Roques de García walk usually work better.

e.l: How high is the Teide?
e.a: 📏 3,715 m: the highest point in Spain and the highest peak in the Atlantic. Measured from the ocean floor it goes beyond 7,000 m, which puts it among the tallest volcanoes in the world counting from its base.

e.l: Getting out of the South airport?
e.a: ✈️ From Tenerife South airport (TFS) there are direct buses: the 10 to Santa Cruz, the 40 express to Los Cristianos and Costa Adeje, and the 343 towards Puerto de la Cruz and the North airport. There are taxis at the door and private transfers too. You pay the driver in cash or by bank card; check the day’s timetable on titsa.com.

e.l: And from the North airport?
e.a: ✈️ Tenerife North airport (TFN, Los Rodeos) is ten minutes from La Laguna. Airport express buses run to Santa Cruz and La Laguna, lines 20 and 30, and the 343 heads south and to Puerto de la Cruz. The tram does not enter the terminal, but it links La Laguna with Santa Cruz every few minutes.

k: how do i pay the bus
e.l: How do the buses work?
e.a: 🚌 The buses are run by TITSA and reach almost the whole island. You can pay the driver in cash with small notes, tap a contactless bank card on many routes, or use the ten+ card, which is noticeably cheaper on intercity journeys. I can tell you which line serves you and where the stop is; for the exact times of the day, titsa.com.

e.l: Is the ten+ card worth it?
e.a: 💳 The ten+ is the island’s transport card: you buy and top it up at stations, kiosks and machines, and there is a mobile version too. It pays off as soon as you make a few intercity journeys, because the discount against single tickets is large. You tap on boarding and, on long routes, when getting off as well.

e.l: Do I need a rental car?
e.a: 🚗 If you are going to stay around the coast and the towns, the bus covers it easily. If you want Anaga, Teno, the inland villages or a viewpoint at sunrise, rent one: there are places public transport barely reaches, and at awkward times. Plenty of people mix it: bus most days, car for two or three.

e.l: What is driving like here?
e.a: 🛣️ Driving is fine, but the island is vertical: fast motorways on the coast, the TF-1 in the south and the TF-5 in the north, and mountain roads full of bends where 40 km can take well over an hour. Use low gears downhill, watch for cyclists and northern fog, and do not trust the time your sat nav gives you.

e.l: Where do I park?
e.a: 🅿️ In the cities there is paid blue-zone parking on weekdays and public car parks in the centre. In the well-known villages and viewpoints, arrive before ten or go at sunset: by mid-morning there is nothing left. Never park on a yellow line or on the bends by the viewpoints: the tow truck is quick. On the map, the Car parks category has car parks around the island: their pop-up tells you whether they are free or roughly what an hour costs, with the date of the price. It does not show free spaces live.

e.l: How long between places?
e.a: ⏱️ Rough guide, by car: Costa Adeje to Santa Cruz, a good hour on the motorway; Costa Adeje to the Teide, an hour and a half; Santa Cruz to Puerto de la Cruz, about 45 minutes; Santa Cruz to deep Anaga, an hour and a half even though it looks next door on the map. For the real route from where you are, tap «🚗 Get there by car» in any place’s pop-up: it opens in Google Maps or, on an iPhone, in Apple Maps.

e.l: How does the tram work?
e.a: 🚋 The tram links Santa Cruz with La Laguna, line 1, and has a second route towards La Cuesta and Tíncer, line 2. It is the easiest way to move between the two cities and saves you the TF-5 jam. You pay with a ten+ card or a ticket from the platform machine, before boarding.

e.l: Taxis? Is there Uber?
e.a: 🚕 Taxis are white, metered, with airport and night surcharges; you take them at a rank, by phone or through your hotel, and in tourist areas there are ranks everywhere. Ride-hailing apps only work in some areas and with a small fleet, so do not count on them as plan A. For an excursion, agree a fixed price before getting in.

e.l: How do I reach another island?
e.a: ⛴️ Ferries to La Gomera leave from Los Cristianos, under an hour on the fast service, and there are sailings to La Palma and El Hierro too. For Gran Canaria you sail from Santa Cruz. Book online, and further ahead still if you are taking the car. Rough seas cancel crossings, so confirm before you set off.

e.l: Can I reach the Teide without a car?
e.a: 🚌🌋 Yes. Two tourist routes climb to the National Park: the 342 from Costa Adeje and the 348 from Puerto de la Cruz, with one morning departure and an afternoon return. Inside the park the 341 links Portillo, Montaña Blanca, the cable car and the Parador. Not every travel pass is valid on these routes, and you are tied to the single return: check the day’s timetable on titsa.com.

e.l: How do I get to Masca?
e.a: 🚌 To see the village, route 355 climbs up from Santiago del Teide and from Buenavista del Norte; parking up there is minimal, so the bus is the better idea anyway. For the gorge descent it is compulsory: you can only get in via the 355 transfer from Santiago del Teide, leaving the car at the cemetery car park, and arriving by private vehicle means you are not allowed to start.

k: is there a train in tenerife
e.l: Is there a train or metro?
e.a: 🚆 There is no train on Tenerife. The closest thing is the tram between Santa Cruz and La Laguna. For the rest of the island the bus network is the backbone, and for rural areas and odd hours, a car.

e.l: Can I rent a bike or scooter?
e.a: 🚲 Yes, you can rent bikes, e-bikes and scooters in the resort areas and at the harbours. The island is a serious road-cycling destination, with long climbs towards the Teide; for getting around town, the electric one earns its keep on the hills. Helmets are compulsory on a scooter, and on a bike outside built-up areas too.

e.l: Can I see the island in a day?
e.a: 🗺️ You can drive right round, but you end up seeing the viewpoints through the window. With one day, pick one axis: the Teide and Vilaflor, or Anaga and La Laguna, or the north coast from Garachico to Icod. Use the app’s planner to chain stops without overdoing the hours or the hairpins.

e.l: Are there tolls?
e.a: 🛣️ No tolls: both motorways, the TF-1 in the south and the TF-5 in the north, are free. What does cost money is parking in town centres. And in high season the TF-1 clogs up around the south in the late afternoon, so leave a margin if you are heading to the airport.

e.l: Is my driving licence valid?
e.a: 🪪 With an EU licence you drive with no paperwork at all. If yours is from outside the EU, rental companies usually ask for an international permit alongside it, but each company sets its own rule: confirm with them before you fly, not at the desk on arrival.

e.l: Where do I get fuel?
e.a: ⛽ Fuel is noticeably cheaper than on the mainland because the Canaries have their own tax regime. There are petrol stations all along the coast and in the midlands, but none inside the National Park or deep in Anaga: go up with a full tank. They are all on the map under their own category, and at the top, ⛽ uses your location to show the cheapest ones within 5, 10 or 20 km: petrol 95 and diesel, at the official price from the Spanish Ministry.

e.l: Which villages are worth it?
e.a: 🏘️ The ones that never disappoint: La Orotava for its mansions and carved balconies, Garachico for the sea and the lava, La Laguna for the old town, Masca and Taganana for the landscape, Vilaflor for the altitude and Candelaria for the basilica facing the Atlantic. Tell me your area and I will sort them by distance.

e.l: What to see in La Laguna?
e.a: 🏛️ It is a World Heritage site: the first unwalled colonial city, with a layout later copied across the Americas. Wander on foot among mansions with inner courtyards, climb the Concepción tower and eat tapas along Calle Herradores and the market. From Santa Cruz the tram gets you there in twenty minutes.

e.l: What to see in La Orotava?
e.a: 🌺 The town of grand houses with pine-wood balconies and courtyards full of flowers. Do not miss the Casa de los Balcones, the Concepción church and the valley view from the Humboldt lookout. At Corpus Christi the streets are carpeted with flowers and sand from the Teide, and it is worth the trip.

e.l: What to see in Garachico?
e.a: ⚓ It was the island’s great port until the 1706 eruption half buried it; out of that lava came the natural pools of El Caletón. Today it is a quiet town with the San Miguel castle, squares with a dragon tree and good swimming when the sea allows. A perfect half day, better on a weekday.

e.l: What to see in Santa Cruz?
e.a: 🏙️ The capital is far livelier than visitors expect: Calatrava’s Auditorio, the Plaza de España, the Nuestra Señora de África market, the TEA art centre, the Palmetum built on a former landfill, and Las Teresitas beach ten minutes away. Plus the best shopping on the island.

e.l: When is the Carnival?
e.a: 🎭 The one in Santa Cruz is among the biggest in the world: the gala where the Carnival Queen is chosen, murga choirs, comparsa dance troupes and whole nights of dancing in the street. It falls in February or March depending on Lent: in the app, at the top, «🎉 Festivals & traditions» gives you the date of the next one, worked out each year from Easter. It ends with the Burial of the Sardine, and Puerto de la Cruz has its own version. If you are here, wear a costume: everyone does.

e.l: Any festivals this month?
e.a: 🎉 Every town has its patron saint and its romería, the festival in the saint’s honour, so there is nearly always something on. The big ones are Carnival, the Corpus Christi in La Orotava, the Virgin of Candelaria in August and San Andrés in late November, when the new wine is opened. In the app, at the top, «🎉 Festivals & traditions» lists the island’s big festivals by their next date, with the ones that move each year already worked out and «Soon» on those in the next three weeks; tap one and the map takes you there.

e.l: What is a romería?
e.a: 🐂 It is a town’s festival in honour of its patron saint: ox-drawn carts, traditional dress, folk bands playing and neighbours handing out wine, potatoes and meat to whoever walks past. You do not pay and you do not need an invitation. You walk in, say hello and accept what you are offered, which is half the fun.

e.l: Who were the Guanches?
e.a: 🗿 They were the island’s inhabitants before the Castilian conquest: shepherds of Berber origin who lived in caves, organised themselves into menceyatos (kingdoms) and mummified their dead. Tenerife was the last island to fall, in 1496. To see it up close, the Museum of Nature and Archaeology in Santa Cruz keeps the mummies.

e.l: Which museums are worth it?
e.a: 🖼️ The essentials: the Museum of Nature and Archaeology for the Guanche mummies, the TEA for contemporary art, the Casa del Vino in El Sauzal and the History Museum in La Laguna. Opening hours and free-entry days change often, so confirm them before turning up.

e.l: Where are the local markets?
e.a: 🧺 The farmers’ markets are the best weekend stop: Tacoronte, La Laguna, Güímar or the Nuestra Señora de África market in Santa Cruz, which opens daily. Days and hours vary by municipality, so confirm before setting off. Go early and take cash.

e.l: Where can I see whales?
e.a: 🐬 There are resident pilot whales and bottlenose dolphins all year in the sea strip between Teno and Rasca, one of the best places in the world to see them. Boats leave from Los Cristianos, Puerto Colón and Los Gigantes. Pick an operator with the Barco Azul mark, which certifies respectful watching, and do not get in the water with them.

e.l: What if I only have one day?
e.a: 🗓️ I would drive up to the Teide early via Vilaflor, have lunch around La Orotava and drop down to Garachico or Puerto de la Cruz at sunset. It makes a complete day and you get three different islands in one: the volcanic summit, the green valley and the north coast. I can chain the stops in the planner for you.

e.l: What about 3, 5 or 7 days?
e.a: 🗺️ With three days: the Teide, Anaga and a day on the south coast. With five, add Teno with Masca and Garachico, plus a day on the northern beaches. With seven, fit in La Gomera by ferry and one unplanned day in La Laguna or Santa Cruz. Save the places to favourites and I will sort them by distance so you do not cross the island twice.

e.l: Is La Gomera worth a day trip?
e.a: ⛴️ Worth it if you get up early: in under an hour you are in San Sebastián, with time to go up to the Garajonay National Park, eat in a village in the north and come back in the afternoon. Book the return for the same day and bear in mind that rough seas cancel crossings: if being stranded would ruin things, sleep over instead.

e.l: Where can I dive or snorkel?
e.a: 🤿 The dive centres cluster in the south, with mild water all year and good visibility: around Las Galletas, Los Cristianos and Radazul. For snorkelling without tanks, the natural pools at low tide and the sheltered coves of the south. In the north the sea calls the shots far more than it looks from the shore.

e.l: Where can I paraglide?
e.a: 🪂 The island is excellent for flying, with classic launch sites above the Orotava valley and around Adeje. You fly tandem with a pilot, so no experience is needed. The flight depends on the day’s wind: book with some slack and expect them to move your time or your launch site.

e.l: Where can I kayak or paddleboard?
e.a: 🛶 In the south, where the sea is calmest: Los Cristianos, Playa Paraíso, Los Gigantes and the Adeje coast, where you can easily run into turtles. You rent by the hour or go with a guide, who will also take you into the coastal caves. In the north, only with a flat sea and only if you know what you are doing.

e.l: Is there any nightlife?
e.a: 🌙 Depends what you are after. Las Américas and Costa Adeje hold the tourist nightlife, with clubs and bars running late. Santa Cruz and La Laguna have the local scene, with the bar district downtown and terraces full of people. People go out late here: at weekends things get going from midnight onwards.

e.l: Where are the golf courses?
e.a: ⛳ There are about a dozen courses, most in the south and a few in the north with views of the Teide and the sea. You can play all year, which is exactly why people come in winter. In the hotter months, book an early tee time. They are on the map under their own category, with directions.

e.l: What is there to do on a Sunday?
e.a: ☀️ On Sunday the island heads for the countryside: recreation areas with barbecues, packed guachinches, a romería (a patron-saint festival) if one falls that weekend and farmers markets in the morning. Many shops close, but restaurants, beaches and trails are at their best. It is the best day to see the island in local mode, and the worst for shopping.

e.l: Any trips without a car?
e.a: 🚌 Perfectly possible. Buses reach the Teide, Masca, Anaga and nearly every village, and from the south there are organised excursions that pick you up at your hotel. What changes is the rhythm: you are tied to the return timetable, so check the last departure before you set off and do not cut it fine.

e.l: What currency is used?
e.a: 💶 The euro. You can pay by card almost everywhere, even for small amounts. Still carry some cash for guachinches, street markets, village car parks and the odd taxi. Cash machines are easy to find, but watch the fees on the ones in tourist areas.

e.l: Can I drink the tap water?
e.a: 🚰 It is drinkable and monitored, but since much of it is desalinated or heavily mineralised, the taste puts people off and almost everyone, locals included, drinks bottled. For cooking and washing it is perfectly fine. On hikes, only refill at springs marked as drinkable.

e.l: What plugs are used?
e.a: 🔌 The European two-round-pin ones, types C and F, at 230 volts and 50 hertz. Coming from the UK, Ireland or outside Europe, bring an adapter: you can buy one at the airport or in supermarkets, but it costs more. Modern chargers handle the voltage without a transformer.

e.l: What documents do I need?
e.a: 🛂 The Canaries are Spain and Schengen territory: coming from the European Union, an ID card or passport is enough and there is no border check. From outside, a passport and, depending on your nationality, a visa or prior authorisation. Requirements change, so confirm them with a Spanish consulate before you fly.

e.l: What time zone is this?
e.a: 🕐 The Canaries run one hour behind mainland Spain and central Europe, and match the UK and Portugal. The clock change happens at the same time as in the rest of the European Union. It is the detail that catches people out on arrival: if you flew from Madrid, put your watch back.

e.l: Can I manage without Spanish?
e.a: 🗣️ No problem. The language is Spanish, but English is widespread in the resort areas and you will hear plenty of German in the north too. Inland it thins out, though gestures and a friendly face solve everything. People here help before you even ask.

e.l: Any Canarian words to know?
e.a: 🗨️ The ones you will hear most: guagua is the bus, papas are potatoes, cotufas are popcorn, millo is sweetcorn, un fisco means a tiny bit, and you already know guachinche. You will also notice people use «ustedes» where mainland Spain says «vosotros», and nobody pronounces the final s.

e.l: Is there wifi? Do I need an eSIM?
e.a: 📶 Wifi is available in accommodation, bars and many public spaces. Mobile coverage is good all along the coast and in the towns, and non-existent at the bottom of the ravines and in parts of Anaga and Teno. From the European Union you use your own data at no extra cost; otherwise a local eSIM is worth it.

e.l: What should I pack?
e.a: 🧳 Summer clothes for the coast, comfortable shoes with grip, swimwear and high-factor sun cream. Add a light jacket for the evenings and something properly warm if you are going up the Teide, even in August. If you plan to walk, bring mountain footwear; flip-flops are no use on the trails.

k: how many days do i need
e.l: How many days do I need?
e.a: 📆 A week is ideal and lets you see the island without rushing. Five days works well if you avoid wasting time crossing from end to end. With three you are tight: pick two areas and forget the rest. Less than that is a stopover, not a trip.

e.l: What are the shop hours?
e.a: 🕙 Small shops usually open in the morning, close at midday and reopen in the afternoon; shopping centres and large stores stay open all day. Many shops close on Sundays, except in the resort areas. Hours vary by season and by municipality, so check before you drive across the island.

e.l: What is the IGIC?
e.a: 🧾 It is the Canaries’ own indirect tax, replacing VAT and noticeably lower. That is why electronics, perfume, tobacco and spirits come out cheaper than on the mainland. Refund conditions for travellers change, so ask in the shop as you pay and keep the receipt.

e.l: Is Tenerife expensive?
e.a: 💰 Cheaper than most European sun destinations, largely because the IGIC is lower than mainland VAT. What pushes the spend up is the area: the tourist seafront and the theme parks. Away from those, eating, getting around by bus and the beach are inexpensive, and the landscape costs nothing.

e.l: How does the app work?
e.a:
ℹ️ Tenerife GO in a nutshell:
• The map: tap a marker to see what it is, its opening hours if it has them and how to get there by car or bus; on the coast, the sea conditions too

• At the bottom: Home, Favorites, Routes, SOS for emergencies, this Assistant and Account, which opens your profile
• The app tour is always in the map legend, at the bottom left: «Take the tour»
Ask me about any feature and I will explain it.

e.l: How do I save a place to favourites?
e.a: ⭐ In the pop-up of any place, tap «Add to favourites». At the bottom, Favorites shows only the places you have saved on the map, with a counter. Without an account they stay on this phone; if you sign in, they are also saved in the cloud and you have them on any device.

e.l: How do I mark a place as visited?
e.a: ✅ In the pop-up of every place there is «○ Mark visited»: tap it and it turns into «✓ Visited». It counts towards your achievements 🏆 and is saved on this phone. If you mark it while you are there, within 500 m, your phone checks it with its location and shows «✓ Visit verified»: 10 verified visits unlock the Tenerife avatars in your profile. Your position is neither stored nor sent.

e.l: How do achievements work?
e.a: 🏆 You unlock achievements by marking places as visited: the more you mark, the more you earn, and there is a special one for the summit of the Teide. Tap the trophy 🏆 on the right of the map to see the ones you have and how many places you have visited. In your profile, «Your island» also shows your stamps and how many places you still need for the next one.

e.l: Can I listen to a place’s description?
e.a: 🔊 Yes. In the pop-up of every place, «▶ Listen» reads out the name and the description, in the language you have set and with your phone’s voice. If your phone has no voice for that language, the button does not appear; if you hear nothing, turn the volume up.

e.l: Does it work offline?
e.a: 📴 Yes, after opening it with a connection: the first time the app is saved and, the second time, the place details in your language and this assistant too. With no signal, the places and their details, search, the categories, the buses with their stops, the night sky 🔭, the SOS panel and this assistant all keep working. In the map layers you have «Island offline», a map of the whole island that comes inside the app; «Satellite» and «Topo» also keep the areas you have already looked at. In the 🔭, the sky map, the calendar, the catalogue, «Point at the sky» and the satellites, while their data is no more than 7 days old, work offline: open it once with a connection and, in «Where to go», «Before going up to Teide» confirms it is saved; the Wikipedia summaries you open are kept for 30 days. Live content does need a connection: the weather, the sea conditions, the cloud forecast for the night sky, the car route and the webcams.
e.n: 📴 Yes, from the first time you open it. With no signal, the places and their details, search, the categories, the buses with their stops, the night sky 🔭, the SOS panel and this assistant all keep working. In the map layers you have «Island offline», a map of the whole island that comes inside the app; «Satellite» and «Topo» need a connection, as does all live content: the weather, the sea conditions, the cloud forecast for the night sky, the car route and the webcams. In the 🔭, the sky map, the calendar, the catalogue, «Point at the sky» and the satellites, while their data is no more than 7 days old, work offline, and the Wikipedia summaries you open are kept for 30 days.

e.l: How do I install the app?
e.a:
📲 It is not in the app stores: you install it from the browser.
• iPhone: in Safari, tap the Share button (square with arrow) and choose «Add to Home Screen»
• Android: in Chrome, open the ⋮ menu and choose «Install app»
It then sits on your home screen like any other app.
e.n: 📲 It is already installed: it is the app you have open. It updates from the store like any other app, and what changes every day (petrol prices, AEMET warnings, satellites) comes in on its own whenever there is a connection.

e.l: How do I change the language?
e.a: 🌐 Tap the flag, the last button on the top bar, and pick your language: the app comes in {L} languages. The interface, the details of the {N} places, the «Listen» voice and my answers all change.

e.l: How do I search for a place?
e.a: 🔍 Tap the magnifying glass on the left of the map and type the name of the place or a category, with or without accents. As you type, suggestions appear and the map keeps only what matches; if you press Enter and there is a single result, it takes you there and opens its pop-up. The ✕ clears it. You can also ask me: «where is the Drago Milenario?».

e.l: How do I filter by category?
e.a: 🗂️ The categories button on the right of the map opens the filters in tabs: nature and beaches, culture, sport, viewpoints, markets… and also pet-friendly or accessible places. Each category shows how many places it has. Tap several and the map shows only those; press and hold one to keep just that one. «Show all» removes the filter. You can also ask me: «viewpoints».

e.l: What does the dice do?
e.a: 🎲 It takes you to a random place and opens its pop-up. If you have categories selected, the surprise comes from them: with «Viewpoints» on, you get a viewpoint.

e.l: What do I see when I tap a place?
e.a: 📍 Tapping a marker opens its pop-up: what it is and its description in your language, opening hours and phone number if it has them, safety notes ⚠️ if there are any and, on the coast, the sea conditions. Below are «Add to favourites», «Share», «▶ Listen», «○ Mark visited», «🚏 How to get there by bus» and «🚗 Get there by car». «See full description» opens the complete details.

e.l: Where can I see today’s weather?
e.a: 🌡️ At the top, the thermometer opens «☀️ Where is it sunny now?»: the live weather in six areas of the island, from best to worst, and the time of sunset; here it can rain in one village and be sunny in the next. The wave 🌊 shows the sea conditions by coast and, in «Swim here today», up to three beaches based on the current sea and wind; the pop-up of every coastal place shows the sea conditions at that exact spot. If AEMET has warnings in force for Tenerife, the wave has a yellow, orange or red dot and, when you open it, they come first; in the thermometer they are at the bottom. Tap one to read it in full. If the warning is for coastal events, «Swim here today» leaves out the beaches on that coast and, in the pop-up of every place on that coast, «The sea here» carries «⚠️ AEMET»: open it and the warning comes first. It needs a connection.

e.l: What are the ⚠️ notes on some places?
e.a: ⚠️ Some places carry their own safety note in their pop-up: rough sea and currents, high mountain, demanding route, unfenced edges, forest area with fire risk or narrow mountain road. Read it before you go.

e.l: How do I plan a route from A to B?
e.a: 🧭 In Routes, at the bottom, «A→B» tab: choose the start and the destination by tapping the map, typing an address or using GPS, and press «Calculate route». It gives you the minutes and kilometres by car and, by bus, the whole journey: the walk to the stop, the line and its minutes (with a change if it saves time) and the walk at the end; if no bus runs at that hour, it tells you the times of the lines that link the two points. Once the route is calculated, «📥 GPX» downloads it to open in another map app. To drive to a specific place, its pop-up has «🚗 Get there by car».

e.l: Can you help me plan my day?
e.a: ✨ In Routes, at the bottom, «Plan your day» tab: say how much time you have, what you fancy (nature, beach, culture, food… one or several), whether you prefer the north or the south (or don’t mind) and how you are getting around (car, bus, on foot or bike), and it puts together an itinerary ordered by distance, with a lunch break if it is half a day or the whole day. On each stop, «🔄 Another» swaps it for another and ✕ removes it; 🔀 redoes the whole thing. You can save it to «Day Route» or to Favorites, share it, or download it with «📥 Download day route (GPX)».

k: how to get there by bus
e.l: Which bus takes me to a place?
e.a: 🚏 In the pop-up of every place, «🚏 How to get there by bus» shows the stops closest to it and the lines that call at each one. Tap a stop to see its line on the map. From where you are: in Routes, turn on GPS and tap the blue dot, which has the same button with the stops near you; and for the whole journey by bus, the «A→B» tab. Times for the day are on titsa.com.

e.l: Do I need an account?
e.a: 👤 No: the app is the same without an account. At the bottom, «Account» opens your profile, which works without an account: everything stays on this phone. If you want one, tap «Sign up or log in» and sign up with email and password: your favourites are also saved in the cloud and you get them back on another device, and your profile and progress too, but only if you also turn that on in the profile.

e.l: How do I share a place?
e.a: 📤 In the pop-up of every place, tap «Share»: your phone’s share menu opens (WhatsApp, email…). If your phone does not have one, the text with the link is copied and you get a notice.

e.l: Where is the Canarian glossary?
e.a: 📖 In the fiestas panel 🎉 at the top, the «📚 Speak like a Canarian» button opens up local words with their meaning: guagua, chacho, ños, papas arrugadas, mojo, guachinche…

e.l: What do I do if something fails?
e.a:
🔧 Try this:
1. Close the app and open it again, or reload the page
2. If it was something live (the weather, the sea, a route), check that you have a connection
3. If you see «New version available», tap «Reload»
Still the same? Write to Jerome with the button below and tell him what happened.

e.l: What is in the shop?
e.a: 🛍️ The shop is not available for now. If you have a business in Tenerife and would like to appear in the app, write to tenerife.go.app@gmail.com.

e.l: Sort my favourites by distance
e.a: 📍 Ask me like this: «sort my favourites by distance». I put them in order from where you are and without going back and forth, so you do not cross the island twice. If you do not let me know where you are, I start from the one at one end. The distances are in a straight line, not by road.

e.l: What can I see in the sky tonight?
e.a: 🔭 At the top, the telescope opens «Tenerife night sky». In «Tonight» you get the night index, your guided night, when full darkness begins, the Moon, the planets, the Space Station passes and the Milky Way, with the cloud forecast; in «Calendar», the coming meteor showers, eclipses, planets, Moon phases and satellites; in «Catalog», stars, clusters and galaxies by whether you can see them with the naked eye, binoculars or a telescope; in «Sky map», the sky at the time you choose and «Point at the sky», which tells you which star is in front of you; and in «Where to go», the places to watch from and the National Park rules for the night. Tap any object to see its card. It is calculated on your phone and works offline, except the clouds and Wikipedia; the satellites need data no more than 7 days old. «Red light» tints the screen so it does not dazzle you.

e.l: When are the meteor showers and eclipses?
e.a: 📅 In the 🔭 at the top, «Calendar» tab: the meteor showers with the night of their peak and how the Moon will be; the solar and lunar eclipses with what will be visible from Tenerife and at what time; and also the planets (oppositions and conjunctions), the equinoxes and solstices, the Moon phases and satellite passes, with a filter for each. It is calculated for Izaña, in Canary Islands time. On each event, «Add to my calendar» puts it in your phone’s calendar, which reminds you the day before (for satellites, half an hour before), and with «Remind me in the app» you see it at the top of «Tonight» for the two days before. For a solar eclipse, never without certified ISO 12312-2 glasses or a solar filter in front of the lens.

e.l: How do I delete my account?
e.a: 🗑️ In «Account», at the bottom, once you are signed in: in your profile, below «Log out», tap «Delete account» and confirm with «Yes, delete my account». Your email address, your password, the favourites saved in the cloud and, if you saved them there, your profile and progress are deleted, and it cannot be undone; what is on this phone stays: profile data is deleted with «Delete profile data from this device», and favourites and the rest when you clear the site data in your browser or uninstall the app. If you cannot do it from the app, write to tenerife.go.app@gmail.com from your account’s email address with the subject «Delete my account»: it is deleted within one month at the latest. Notifications are not part of the account: you turn them off in your browser or in your phone’s settings.

e.l: What data does the app keep?
e.a: 🔒 It is all in «Privacy · GDPR», at the bottom of the map, and on the web in «Web version». Your location, only when you turn it on, and it is not stored on any server; the camera and the phone’s orientation, only if you use them in «Point at the sky», in the 🔭, and they never leave your phone; your email address and password, if you create an account; your favourites, in the cloud only with an account; your profile and progress, in your account only if you turn that on; and, if you turn on notifications, your browser’s subscription, with the app’s language. Usage statistics, only if you accept the cookie notice. To delete your account, «Delete your account», right next to it.
e.n: 🔒 It is all in «Privacy · GDPR», at the bottom of the map, and on the web in «Web version». Your location, only when you turn it on, and it is not stored on any server; the camera and the phone’s orientation, only if you use them in «Point at the sky», in the 🔭, and they never leave your phone; your email address and password, if you create an account; your favourites, in the cloud only with an account; and your profile and progress, in your account only if you turn that on. This app has no usage statistics and no cookie notice: Google Analytics is only on the website. To delete your account, «Delete your account», right next to it.

e.l: What does «Sponsored» mean?
e.a: 💼 They are businesses that pay a monthly promotion plan to appear on the map: their pop-up says so, «Sponsored». Everyone sees them the same way, without using your data or advertising cookies, and they do not change the rest of the content.

e.l: Can I get a message every morning?
e.a: 🔔 Yes, with the app installed on your home screen: the third time you open it, it asks «A little nudge each morning?», a line to start the day, with no ads. On Sundays, instead of the line, a tip from the SOS panel on what to do in an emergency; and if Tenerife’s volcanic traffic light changes, a notice with the INVOLCAN bulletin. If you answered «Not now», it does not ask again, but you can turn them on whenever you like with «Turn on notifications» in your profile («Account», at the bottom), even if you are not signed in. On iPhone, first add it to your home screen from Safari. To stop them, go to your phone’s notification settings.
e.n: 🔔 No: this app does not send notifications.

e.l: How do I switch the map to satellite or terrain?
e.a: 🗺️ At the top, the map layers button switches layer with each tap: «Streets», «Satellite», «Topo» (the terrain map, the best one for hiking) and «Island offline», then back to the start; a short notice tells you which one is on. «Island offline» is a map of the whole island that comes inside the app: it works with no signal.

e.l: How do I build my day route?
e.a: 🗓️ In Routes, at the bottom, «Day Route» tab: choose «North», «South» or «Summit» and tap + on the places you want to visit. They are numbered in «My route»: on each stop, 📍 centres it on the map, ℹ️ opens its pop-up and ✕ removes it. With 🗓️+, in «Plan your day», you add that itinerary here. «My route» lasts while the app is open: to keep the places, save them to Favorites.

e.l: How do I see a bus line on the map?
e.a: 🚌 At the top, the bus button opens «Public transport», with the TITSA lines and the tram. Search by line number or stop name and tap a line: it is drawn on the map with its stops. You can turn on several, and the app remembers them. «✈️ TFS South» and «✈️ TFN North» turn on the lines for each airport in one go, and «Getting around» sums up how to pay, taxis and car hire. The official timetables are on titsa.com, linked at the bottom of the panel, and the tram’s on metrotenerife.com.

k: where am i on the map
e.l: How do I see where I am on the map?
e.a: 📍 In Routes, at the bottom, tap «GPS» at the top of the panel: the map shows where you are with a blue dot. Tap the dot and you get the accuracy, «Use as route Origin», which makes it the start in «A→B», and «🚏 How to get there by bus», with the closest stops on foot from where you are. Tap «GPS» again to turn it off. Your location is not stored on any server.

e.l: Can I see only the places the bus goes to?
e.a: 🚏 Yes. First, in the bus button at the top, turn on the lines that suit you. Then, in the categories button, at the very bottom, switch on «Bus-accessible only»: the map keeps the places less than 500 m from a stop on those lines. It works together with the categories: with «Beaches» on, you get the beaches with a bus nearby.

e.l: Can I download the route as GPX?
e.a: 📥 Yes. In «A→B», once the route is calculated, tap «📥 GPX»; in «Plan your day», under the itinerary, «📥 Download day route (GPX)». Your phone’s share menu opens so you can save it or open it in a map app such as Organic Maps, Wikiloc or Komoot.

e.l: What are the circles with numbers on the map?
e.a: 🔢 They are groups of places: where there are many close together, the map gathers them in a circle showing how many are inside. Tap the circle or zoom in and they split up. The «Legend», at the bottom left of the map, explains each symbol: place, favourite, group, the route with its start (A) and end (B), and your location. «Take the tour» is there too.

e.l: What is in my profile?
e.a: 👤 At the bottom, «Account» opens «Your profile», your traveller’s passport: your avatar and your name or nickname; «Your details», with your height, weight and year of birth, and your BMI, as a guide, with the WHO categories for adults; «Your progress», with the weights and kilometres you log, the 7-day trend and a goal if you want one; «Your island», with your favourites, visited places, achievements and stamps; and the account. Your name, avatar, details and progress are saved on this phone, and in your account only if you turn that on; visited places and achievements always stay on the phone.

e.l: How do I choose my avatar?
e.a: 🎭 In «Your profile», «Choose your avatar»: 235 drawings in 47 collections, one for each language of the app, one for each of 36 European countries and one for Tenerife. Your country’s, your language’s and Tenerife’s are right at the top; «All countries» shows them all, with a search box, and another button picks one at random. The Tenerife one 🌋 unlocks after 10 verified visits, those to places you mark as visited while you are there. You change your name or nickname with the pencil next to it.

e.l: Is my profile saved in the cloud?
e.a: ☁️ Only if you want it to be. When you are signed in, «Your profile» has «Save profile and progress to your account», off to begin with: when you turn it on, it explains what is saved and, since weight and height are health data, nothing is uploaded unless you tap «I agree». You can turn it on from age 16, once your birth year is entered in «Your details», and verified visits are never uploaded. If you turn it off, the copy in your account is deleted and everything stays on your phone. «Download profile data» gives you a file with your data, and «Delete profile data from this device» deletes it from your phone, and from your account too if the switch was on; your favourites are not touched.

k: point my phone at the sky
e.l: Which star is that?
e.a: 📱 In the 🔭, «Sky map» tab, tap «Point at the sky» and hold your phone up to the star: whatever sits inside the central circle is named below, and tapping it opens its card. With 📷 the camera image shows in the background, and with 🔍 you search for an object and an arrow leads you to it. A phone compass drifts out of calibration on its own: the first time, a 20-second guide appears, and «Check the compass» corrects it using the Moon, a planet or the brightest star. If you do not allow the motion sensors, you move the sky with your finger. Nothing from the camera or the sensors leaves your phone.

k: what should i look at tonight
what to look at in the sky
e.l: What should I look at tonight, step by step?
e.a: 🧭 In the 🔭, at the top of «Tonight», «Your guided night» lines up that night’s stops, from the easiest to the most subtle: the Moon if it is up, the brightest planets, named stars, the best naked-eye sights, the Milky Way if there is no Moon, a satellite pass and the active meteor shower. For each one it tells you where to look, and «Take me there» opens «Point at the sky» with the arrow on it. «Read aloud» reads them out one by one with your phone’s voices, offline, and leaves you 30 seconds to find each one; «Pause», «Resume» and «Next» control it.

e.l: When can I see the Space Station?
e.a: 🛰️ In the 🔭, «Tonight» has a card, «The Space Station and other satellites», and the «Calendar» has the «Satellites» filter: the passes of the International Space Station, the Chinese Tiangong station and the Hubble telescope visible from Teide over the next seven nights, with the time it appears, where, how high it climbs, how long it lasts and how bright it is. It looks like a bright dot crossing the sky without twinkling. Each pass shows up on the sky map and in «Point at the sky», and with «Add to my calendar» your calendar reminds you half an hour before. Your phone works it out with data renewed every day; Starlink is not included.

e.l: What does the card of each star or planet tell me?
e.a: ✨ In the 🔭, tap any object on the sky map, in «Point at the sky» or in the lists and its card opens: where it is at that moment; what is known about it, worked out from sourced data (how many light years away it is, its colour, how bright it is), and for each planet the NASA figures; when it rises, culminates and sets tonight; «Did you know?», a curious fact with its source, and «Show its path tonight», which draws its path on the sky map or in «Point at the sky». Last comes the Wikipedia summary in your language, kept on your phone for 30 days. Each of the 88 constellations also shows where it comes from and how much sky it covers.

e.l: Where are the planets today?
e.a: 🪐 In the 🔭, near the end of «Tonight», «The solar system today» draws the orbits and where each planet is today, seen from above the Sun, with the Earth and Tenerife; choose «Out to Mars» or «Out to Neptune». Tap a planet and it tells you how far it is from the Sun and from us, how long its light takes to reach us and how many degrees from the Sun it appears; ▶ runs time at a month per second. To see them tonight, use the «Planets» card further up.

e.l: What is the red light for?
e.a: 🔴 In the 🔭, «Red light» tints the whole screen red, not just the panel, so you are not dazzled and keep seeing the stars; while it is on, a slider next to the button turns the brightness down even further, in «Point at the sky» too. If you open the panel at night with white light, the app offers it once. When you reach a dark spot, switch off white lights and let your eyes adapt for about 20 minutes.

e.l: Is it a good night for stargazing?
e.a: ⭐ In the 🔭, at the top of «Tonight», the «Night index» gives a score from 0 to 10, showing how it is worked out: 10 points for a whole dark night without the Moon; time with the Moon up is deducted, depending on how full it is, and the medium and high cloud forecast by Open-Meteo lowers it. It does not count light pollution or wind. «Share» sends it as a picture, and with 📅 you can check it for any other night.

e.l: When is the next full moon?
e.a: 🌕 In the 🔭, «Tonight», the «Moon» card: its phase and how lit it is, when it rises and sets, which constellation it is in, and the dates of the next new moon and the next full moon. In the «Calendar», the «Moon phases» filter has all of them, with their time. New moon gives the darkest nights, the best for the Milky Way; full moon is the best for looking at the Moon itself.

k: when can i see the milky way
e.l: When can I see the Milky Way?
e.a: 🌌 In the 🔭, «Tonight», the «Milky Way» card tells you from what time to what time its brightest part is visible and how high it climbs, or from which night it comes back; you need a spot far from lights, no Moon, and at least 20 minutes for your eyes to adapt. The «For photos» card gives the golden and blue hours in the evening and morning, the zodiacal light in its season and Teide’s triangular shadow at sunrise and sunset.

k: where to set up a telescope
e.l: Where can I set up a telescope at night?
e.a: 🔭 In Teide National Park, the Master Plan for Use and Management (Decree 182/2025) only allows telescopes to be set up at the viewpoints and pedestrian area of La Ruleta, by the Parador and the Cañada Blanca visitor centre; in the cable-car car parks (the one on the TF-21 and the one at the base station); outside the Altavista refuge; in the Minas de San José car parks and at Portillo Alto. At night the only lights allowed are those of moving cars, hand torches and head torches, and laser pointers only on guided observations. Camping, sleeping in a vehicle and parking motorhomes, caravans or campervans are not allowed, except those linked to authorised activities in special-use zones; to spend the night up there, there are bivouac areas that must be booked in advance on Tenerife ON, such as the one on Guajara. Stargazing tours: groups of 30 at most, with an accredited guide. In the app: 🔭, «Where to go», «National Park rules for the night».

k: what to see with a telescope
what can i see with a telescope
e.l: What can I see with binoculars or a telescope?
e.a: 🔭 In the 🔭, «Tonight», «Best of the night» sorts it by instrument («Naked eye», «Binoculars» and «Telescope»), with the time and the direction to look. The «Catalog» has stars, double stars, variables, clusters, nebulae, galaxies and constellations, with a search box and the «High tonight» filter; each object’s level comes from its brightness and how high it climbs from Tenerife. With binoculars (7×50 or 10×50) you can see the Pleiades, the Andromeda Galaxy or Jupiter’s moons; with a telescope, the craters of the Moon, Saturn’s rings or globular clusters. In «Where to go», «What to bring».

e.l: What number do I call in an emergency?
e.a: 🚨 For any emergency, call 112: it is free, works 24 hours a day and answers in Spanish, English, German, French and Italian, and with an interpreter in more than 40 languages. Say where you are as precisely as you can: the name of the trail or the beach and something you can see nearby. If you cannot explain it, in the SOS panel at the bottom, «Show my coordinates» gives you your position to read out, and the 112 Canarias app sends it automatically. For information when it is not an emergency, call 012 (+34 922 470 012), which is not free.

e.l: Is the sea dangerous?
e.a: 🌊 Here the Atlantic is in charge. Always check the flag: green, safe to swim; yellow, swim with caution; red, no swimming. The others are in the pop-up of every beach, under «What does each flag mean?». Where there is no lifeguard, take extra care, and in rough seas stay away from the edge of rocks and rock pools. If a current pulls you, do not swim against it: swim parallel to the shore or float, and call for help by waving your arms. Emergencies: 112. In the SOS panel, «Swimming safely», «Someone in trouble in the water» and «Stings at sea» tell you what to do.

e.l: What is calima?
e.a: 🌫️ Calima is Saharan dust hanging in the air: the sky turns yellowish and air quality gets worse. The Canary Islands Health Department advises drinking water, avoiding physical effort outdoors, not spending long outside and keeping windows closed; if you have asthma or another respiratory or heart condition, and with children and older people, take extra care. If AEMET issues a warning for suspended dust, you will see it in the app: a coloured dot on the wave 🌊 and the warning at the very top when you open it. Also on the AEMET website. And in the SOS panel, «Heat and dust haze».

e.l: What precautions should I take in the mountains?
e.a: 🥾 In the mountains the weather changes fast with altitude. Take plenty of water, a cap, sun protection and something warm; tell someone your route and when you plan to be back; stay on the marked trail and do not go into a ravine if it is raining or about to rain. Before you set off, read the ⚠️ note in the pop-up if there is one and check closures and bookings on tenerifeon.es. If something happens: 112. In the SOS panel, «In the mountains» tells you what to do if there is an accident or you get lost.

e.l: How do I protect myself from the sun?
e.a: ☀️ The Canary Islands have the highest ultraviolet levels in Spain all year round, and clouds do not stop them. The Canary Islands Public Health Department advises SPF 30 or higher (50 or higher when the index is very high), shade, a hat, covering clothes and sunglasses. On the Teide, with the altitude, the sun is even stronger. If someone feels unwell from the heat, get them into the shade and give them water; if it is serious, 112. The UV forecast for each island is on the AEMET website.

e.l: Where is an on-duty pharmacy?
e.a: 💊 Pharmacies have a green cross, and in every area there is always one on duty, on a rota that changes every day. On the map they are in the Pharmacies category, and the pop-up of each one has the «💊 Find today's on-duty pharmacy» link. For an emergency, 112.

e.l: What if I need a doctor?
e.a: 🏥 If you come from the EU, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Switzerland or the United Kingdom, the European Health Insurance Card entitles you to the necessary medical care in the public health system, on the same terms as residents. It does not cover private care or repatriation, so travel insurance is still a good idea; if you come from another country, be sure to take out a policy. The map shows the hospitals with 24-hour emergency departments and the health centres; from the SOS panel, «Hospitals on the map» shows the hospitals in one tap. If it is serious, 112.

e.l: Where can I get help if I suffer violence?
e.a: 🆘 If you are in danger, call 112. 016 helps women 24 hours a day. In Tenerife, the 24-hour Crisis Centre for victims of sexual violence helps women over 16, free of charge and confidentially, also without reporting it, and the Cabildo’s SIAM gives psychological, legal and social support to women who are victims of gender violence, by appointment. You have them on the map, in the «Help & Support» category.

k: what to do in an emergency
e.l: What does the SOS button open?
e.a: 🆘 At the bottom, between Routes and the Assistant, «SOS» opens «Emergencies»: what to do in a volcanic eruption, an earthquake, a tsunami, a fire, a storm or trouble at sea. «What to do if…» has the guides, in groups: if the authorities tell you to act, if someone is taken ill, at sea, the volcano, earthquakes and tsunamis, fire, weather and mountains, and in buildings and on the street. «What is happening now» shows, each with its date: AEMET’s warnings for Tenerife, if there are any; «Alerts from the Government of the Canary Islands», up to three from the last 7 days, with the official headline in Spanish; the colour of the volcanic traffic light in INVOLCAN’s latest weekly bulletin; how many earthquakes IGN has recorded near Tenerife in the last 10 days, and the five most recent; and links to official updates on the situation. A summary appears at the top only when there is something to report: AEMET warnings in force, Government alerts from the last 24 hours, a traffic light that is not green or an earthquake of magnitude 3 or more in the last 24 hours; with that traffic light or that earthquake, the SOS button also shows a dot. «Get ready» has the emergency bag, the family plan, what to know if you are visiting, ES-Alert, the official plans and channels, and «Hospitals on the map». At the very bottom, always, «Call 112». It works offline. The app does not decide whether there is danger: 112 and the authorities do.

e.l: What do I do if there is a volcanic eruption?
e.a: 🌋 In the SOS panel, «The volcanic traffic light» explains the four colours of the Canary Islands volcanic risk plan (PEVOLCA): green, normal activity; yellow, alert; orange, maximum alert; and red, emergency. It can be different in each municipality. People only evacuate when the authorities say so: your town hall announces the routes and the meeting point, and warnings come by ES-Alert, loudspeakers, radio, TV and official social media. What to do is in «You are told to evacuate», «You are told to stay indoors», «Ash is falling» and «There are volcanic gases». Under «What is happening now» you will find the colour from INVOLCAN’s latest weekly bulletin, with its date, and the link to the bulletin; if it is not green, it also appears at the top of the panel and as a dot of that colour on the SOS button. With notifications turned on, you also get a notice when the traffic light changes colour.

e.l: What do I do in an earthquake or a tsunami?
e.a: 🌊 In the SOS panel, «The ground shakes» and «Tsunami». If the ground shakes while you are indoors, drop down, take cover under a sturdy table and hold on to it, away from windows and anything that could fall, and do not use the lift; outdoors, move away from tall buildings, power poles and billboards, and near the sea, away from the shore. Leave the coast straight away if there is an official warning, if you feel a strong or long earthquake near the sea, if the sea pulls back suddenly or if you hear a roar like a train: go on foot as high and as far from the sea as you can, and only go back when the authorities say so. Under «What is happening now» you will find how many earthquakes IGN has recorded near Tenerife in the last 10 days and the five most recent, with their magnitude and area; one of magnitude 3 or more in the last 24 hours also appears at the top of the panel and puts a dot on the SOS button. More earthquakes do not mean there will be an eruption.

e.l: What do I do if someone is taken ill?
e.a: ⛑️ Call 112 and put your phone on speaker: they will tell you what to do until help arrives. In the SOS panel, «First aid» guides you with the 2025 guidelines of the European Resuscitation Council: if the person does not respond and is not breathing normally, push hard and fast in the centre of the chest, 100 to 120 times a minute, and use a defibrillator if there is one; if they are breathing normally, turn them on their side, unless they have fallen from a height or taken a hard blow; it also covers what to do if someone is choking, bleeding heavily, may be having a heart attack or a stroke, or has been burnt. At sea, «Someone in trouble in the water»; in the heat, «Heat and dust haze».

k: what to pack for an emergency
e.l: What goes in an emergency bag?
e.a: 🎒 In the SOS panel, under «Get ready», «The emergency bag» lists fifteen items, taken from the Civil Protection guide for families and the official advice for a volcanic eruption: documents, medicines, your phone with its charger and a power bank, a battery radio, a torch, a whistle, water (at least 1.5 litres per person per day, for 3 days), food that keeps, masks and sealed goggles, a first-aid kit, warm clothes and a change of clothes, some cash and spare keys, and things for children and pets. You can tick what you already have: it is saved only on this phone. Check it every six months. Next to it, «The family plan»: a meeting point, a contact person and a house outside the risk areas.

e.l: What is ES-Alert?
e.a: 📲 It is the Civil Protection alert system: it reaches phones that are switched on and have coverage in the affected area, with no app or sign-up, and it sounds even on silent; in aeroplane mode it does not arrive. If it says SIMULACRO or PRUEBA (drill or test), it is an exercise: read it and do not call 112. If it is real, read it all and follow its instructions; if you are driving, park somewhere safe first. Do not call 112 to ask questions: get information from 112 Canarias on social media, from the radio or TV, or by calling 012. It also reaches foreign phones that are set up correctly, in Spanish and sometimes in another language, and it will never ask you for personal details. It is in the SOS panel, «ES-Alert messages».

e.l: What is the typical food?
e.a: 🍽️ What you cannot leave without trying: papas arrugadas with red and green mojo, gofio, local cheese, fresh fish, goat meat and conejo en salmorejo (rabbit in a spicy marinade), and for dessert bienmesabe or quesillo. To drink, local wine or a barraquito. On the map, the Gastronomy category.

e.l: What is a guachinche?
e.a: 🍷 A guachinche is a place where the winegrower sells wine from their own harvest, along with a few traditional dishes. The Canary Islands Government regulates them: they can only open for a few months a year and close when the wine runs out, so the one you liked may not be open. On the map they are under Gastronomy, and most of them are in the north.

e.l: What are papas arrugadas with mojo?
e.a: 🥔 Small potatoes boiled with lots of salt until the skin wrinkles; you eat them skin and all, dipped in mojo: the red one, or picón, made with peppers, and the green one, with coriander. It is the Canarian dish par excellence.

e.l: What is gofio?
e.a: 🌾 Gofio is flour made from toasted cereals, and the ancient Canarians already ate it. It is eaten savoury, in escaldón (mixed with broth), and sweet, in milk or in desserts.

e.l: What is a barraquito?
e.a: ☕ The island’s coffee, served in a glass in layers: condensed milk, liqueur, coffee, frothed milk, cinnamon and lemon peel. If you do not want alcohol, ask for it without liqueur.

e.l: What wine is made in Tenerife?
e.a: 🍇 Tenerife has five designations of origin of its own: Abona, Tacoronte-Acentejo, Valle de Güímar, Valle de La Orotava and Ycoden-Daute-Isora. The Casa del Vino in El Sauzal brings them all together and is a good place to start. And at San Andrés, at the end of November, the new wine is opened.

e.l: What cheese is typical?
e.a: 🧀 Goat’s cheese rules on the island: fresh, semi-cured, cured or smoked. You will see it grilled with mojo or with palm honey. Local cheeses are sold at the farmers’ markets.

e.l: What is the weather like in Tenerife?
e.a: 🌤️ An island of microclimates: the trade winds leave more cloud and more green in the north, while the south and west are drier and sunnier. In summer the low morning clouds of the «panza de burro» are typical in the north; on the summit it is properly cold and in winter it can snow. If it is cloudy where you are, crossing the island often changes that. For today’s weather, area by area, use the thermometer 🌡️ at the top.

e.l: When is the best time to come?
e.a: 📅 Any time: on the coast the climate is mild all year. What changes is the plan: in summer, more heat and warmer sea; in winter, possible snow on the Teide; in February or March, Carnival. If you want to climb to the Teide peak, check early that there are permit places.

e.l: Should I stay in the north or the south?
e.a: 🧭 It depends on what you are after. The south (Costa Adeje, Los Cristianos, El Médano) has the most reliable sun and the easiest beaches. The north (Puerto de la Cruz, La Orotava, Garachico) is greener and more Canarian, with the guachinches close by. The island is not big: wherever you sleep, the other side is a day trip away.

e.l: What beaches are there?
e.a: 🏖️ There are beaches of black volcanic sand, golden sand and pebbles, and they are very different depending on the coast: in the south, more sheltered and with facilities; in the north and in Anaga, wilder and with bigger waves. Before swimming, check each beach’s pop-up for its ⚠️ note if it has one, the flag and the sea conditions.

e.l: Where are there natural pools?
e.a: 💧 They are seawater pools among the lava, almost all on the north coast. Swim only when the sea is calm, get in by the steps and wear water shoes, because the rock is sharp. In rough seas, stay away from the edge. Each pool’s pop-up has its safety note and the sea conditions.

e.l: What can I do with kids?
e.a: 👨‍👩‍👧 The map has the Family and Animals categories: water parks and animal parks, hands-on museums, beaches with calm water… They can go up the Teide by cable car, bearing in mind the cold and the altitude. And in Routes, «Plan your day», choose Family and the app puts the plan together.

k: what to do if it rains
e.l: What can I do if it rains?
e.a: 🌧️ First, cross the island: if it rains in the north, the south is usually sunny. If you would rather be indoors, go for museums: the Museum of Nature and Archaeology in Santa Cruz or the Museum of Science and the Cosmos in La Laguna. The Cueva del Viento lava tube in Icod is visited by booking. On the map, the Museums category.

e.l: What can I do for free?
e.a: 🆓 Plenty: the beaches, the viewpoints, the old towns of La Laguna, La Orotava or Garachico, the markets and most trails, including those in Teide National Park, which has no entrance fee. Some trails need booking in advance even though they are free, like the Bosque Encantado in Anaga; the Teide peak trail also needs an authorisation.

e.l: Are there easy trails?
e.a: 🥾 To start with: the Sendero de los Sentidos at Cruz del Carmen (Anaga), with short loops and one adapted for wheelchairs; the Roques de García loop in Teide National Park; and the coastal walk from Almáciga to Roque de las Bodegas, also in Anaga. Tap each one on the map to see its details.

e.l: Can I fly a drone?
e.a: 🚁 Very carefully: in Teide National Park and the other protected natural areas you cannot fly a drone for leisure without authorisation, and the Guardia Civil issues fines. For everything else, check the AESA rules (aesa.gob.es) before take-off: registration, insurance and no-fly zones, such as near airports.

e.l: Where can I camp?
e.a: 🏕️ Only in authorised areas: camping outside them is forbidden and punishable by a fine. The Cabildo has camping areas in the hills, free with prior authorisation. On the map they are in the Campsites category. They can close when there is a fire risk, so check their status before you go. In Teide National Park, camping, sleeping in a vehicle and parking motorhomes, caravans or campervans are not allowed either, except those linked to authorised activities in special-use zones; to spend the night up there, there are bivouac areas, which must be booked in advance on Tenerife ON, and the Altavista refuge.

e.l: Where does bus 111 go?
e.a: 🚌 The 111 links the Santa Cruz Intercambiador with the Costa Adeje bus station, by way of Los Cristianos. At the top, in the buses button 🚌, search for it by its number and tap it: it is drawn on the map with all its stops. The day’s times are on titsa.com.

e.l: What should I know about the Teide?
e.a: 🌋 At 3,715 m the Teide is the highest point in Spain, and entry to the National Park is free. The cable car goes up to La Rambleta, at about 3,555 m, with no permit; the last stretch to the crater needs a prior authorisation, booked on Tenerife ON and not included in the ticket. Up there it is cold and there is less oxygen: wrap up and go slowly. Without a car, buses 342 and 348 get you there.

e.l: What to see in Anaga?
e.a: 🌿 Anaga Rural Park, in the north-east, is a Biosphere Reserve covered in laurel forest. To start, the Cruz del Carmen Visitor Centre and the Sendero de los Sentidos; then the hamlets and wild beaches of Taganana, Benijo and Almáciga. The Bosque Encantado (El Pijaral) can only be visited with a free prior permit: details in its entry. It is often misty and the ground is slippery: wear good shoes.

e.l: How do I get to Punta de Teno?
e.a: 🌅 Punta de Teno is the island’s north-western tip, with its lighthouse and views of La Gomera. The last stretch of road is regulated: during the regulated hours you cannot drive up in a private car, and you go on the shuttle bus from Buenavista del Norte. Check the current times before you go.

e.l: What is the Barranco del Infierno like?
e.a: 💦 It is a trail in Adeje that goes up the ravine to a waterfall, in a protected area with a limited number of visitors per day. Booking is compulsory at barrancodelinfierno.es; so is the helmet, which they give you there. It closes on rainy or windy days. Take water and hiking shoes.
